verdicts.reason: A shrinks the Claim the Deal button until it is the smallest element on the canvas, buried beneath the sale ribbon. Its legal text sits close to the subhead's size, and the logo is tiny, so the hierarchy is inverted. B keeps a strong CTA and a prominent ribbon, but its headline leaves 'last' orphaned on its own line, and the legal text is jammed between the subhead and the oversized button.

A shrinks the LONGEST DAY SALE ribbon to a tiny, barely legible tag below the CTA, so the sale message becomes trivial and the reading order is wrong. It also has the orphaned 'last' and cramped legal text. B shares the orphan and the cramped legal text but keeps the sale ribbon prominent at the top and the CTA strong.

A sets the headline on one clean line, keeps the legal line small and subordinate, and gives the CTA good weight. However, the sale ribbon is shrunk and wedged awkwardly between the legal text and the button, and the logo is undersized. B keeps the ribbon prominent but has the orphaned 'last', cramped legal text butting against an oversized CTA, and a lopsided header with the ribbon left and the logo right.

A breaks the reading order: the headline and legal text sit at the very top, there is a big dead gap above the bottle, and the Solstice logo is reduced to a near-invisible mark at the bottom under the CTA, so the brand is lost. B keeps the logo and ribbon prominent and the order logical, though the orphaned 'last' and the cramped legal-to-CTA spacing still need fixing.
